title: When the Summit Wakes
premise: When a government survey team vanishes in the high interior, bush pilot Hazel Oyelaran is the only one close enough to reach them — and the only one who knows the mountains well enough to suspect the truth: the team found something in the ice that others will kill to claim. Racing a well-armed salvage fleet across six tides of melting pass, Hazel is forced into an uneasy alliance with Mara Voss, the survey's presumed-dead geologist, and must choose between the duty that made him a pilot and the love he never planned for. In the end, Hazel brings Mara out alive but burns his plane and the survey's discovery with it, trading his livelihood — and his old life — for the one thing the mountain couldn't take.
about_author: Dominic Sterling is a former bush pilot turned novelist who spent a decade flying cargo and rumors across the northern interior before trading his logbook for a typewriter. His fiction draws on the people, weather, and moral weather of the far country, where survival is a daily negotiation.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Hazel Oyelaran flies medicine and mail into the interior, establishing his solitary, competent life and his rule against attachments. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: quiet contentment shadowed by loneliness — a man who measures life in miles to avoid counting years.

chapters.title: The Quiet Frequency
chapters.summary: A garbled distress transmission from the government survey team cuts off mid-word. Hazel reports it; the authorities are oddly unhurried. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: unease — the first crack in the ordinary, and the sense that someone wants the silence to last.

chapters.title: Gear and No Tracks
chapters.summary: Flying the survey's last known coordinates, Hazel spots the camp: tents standing, equipment intact, no bodies, no tracks in fresh snow. He lands against his better judgment. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve — this wasn't weather, it was people.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: A government man named Aldous Crane arrives and conscripts Hazel: reach the wreck site before the salvage fleet does, by the spring melt — six tides of the pass. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: resentment and duty colliding; Hazel agrees because leaving people unaccounted for is a debt he can't fly away from.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet
chapters.summary: Hazel glimpses the rival convoy — armed, well-funded, moving faster than any legitimate rescue. Crane's story about 'recovering equipment' frays. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening; the race is no longer about rescue.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Ice Cave
chapters.summary: Forced down by weather, Hazel shelters in a cave and finds Mara Voss, the survey geologist — alive, frostbitten, and hiding from her own government. POV: alternating Hazel/Mara. Emotional beat: wary recognition — two survivors of the same lie.

chapters.title: What the Survey Found
chapters.summary: Mara reveals the team discovered a mineral lode of staggering value beneath the glacier — and that the 'survey' was a cover for a private syndicate using Crane as its hand. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: confession as survival; trust begins, grudging and necessary.

chapters.title: First Tide: The Pass Holds
chapters.summary: They fly out ahead of the melt, Mara navigating by memory of the survey's route while the salvage convoy shadows them. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the partnership takes shape — competence becoming intimacy.

chapters.title: The Fuel Ledger
chapters.summary: Crane sabotages Hazel's fuel cache; the numbers no longer work. They must divert to a ghost mining town, costing them a full tide. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the race's first real wound — the price of survival made literal in gallons.

chapters.title: Ghost Town
chapters.summary: In the abandoned town, Mara and Hazel scavenge fuel and, around a stove, trade their histories — her disgraced career, his dead brother, the crash that taught him to keep flying. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love kindling against duty's cold arithmetic.

chapters.title: Second Tide: The Convoy Catches Up
chapters.summary: The salvage fleet's lead plane strafes the strip as they take off. Hazel flies low through a canyon on instinct and nerve. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration fused — he remembers why he flies, and who he's now flying for.

chapters.title: Crane's Offer
chapters.summary: Crane reaches them by radio: give up Mara and the survey data, and Hazel walks away rich and clean. Hazel refuses; Crane promises to bury them both. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the corruption of power laid bare — and Hazel's line drawn.

chapters.title: Third Tide: Mara's Secret
chapters.summary: Mara admits she signed on knowing the syndicate's true purpose — she needed the money and told herself the mountain wouldn't miss what they took. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: guilt and honesty; love tested by the truth it must hold.

chapters.title: The Wreck
chapters.summary: They reach the survey's final camp at the glacier face: the team's plane, wrecked deliberately, and evidence the others were taken — or killed — by Crane's men. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: grief and fury; the race was never a race, it was a cover-up.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide: The Ice Gives
chapters.summary: The melt accelerates; the lode's entrance yawns open, and the syndicate's men arrive by air. Hazel and Mara are pinned at the glacier with the fleet closing. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: cornered — survival now demands sacrifice, not speed.

chapters.title: Fifth Tide: What Power Wants
chapters.summary: Crane lands under a white flag and offers Mara partnership — the syndicate will make her rich and rewrite the survey's dead into heroes. She nearly says yes. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive — power offering absolution.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Glacier
chapters.summary: Hazel, wounded in a scuffle with Crane's men, tells Mara he'll fly her out with nothing — no evidence, no fortune, just her. She chooses him over the syndicate. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved — they choose each other, knowing the cost.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide: Fire on the Ice
chapters.summary: Cornered by the fleet, Hazel torches the survey data and collapses the lode's entrance with fuel charges, burying the discovery. Crane's men open fire as they run for the plane. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the climax — destruction as the only honest inheritance.

chapters.title: The Long Glide
chapters.summary: The plane, riddled and leaking fuel, can't make the pass. Hazel glides it down the river valley in silence, Mara reading the water, until they set it down on a gravel bar and walk out. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: exhausted grace — survival stripped to its essentials.

chapters.title: Crane's Reckoning
chapters.summary: They reach the coast as the syndicate's story collapses — the missing team's families, tipped by Mara's hidden duplicate notes, force an inquiry. Crane is taken, though the syndicate's name never surfaces. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: imperfect justice — the powerful fall, but not all the way.

chapters.title: Ashes and Altitude
chapters.summary: Hazel's plane is written off; his license suspended pending inquiry. Stripped of the miles that defined him, he faces the years he's avoided counting — with Mara beside him. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: loss transformed into beginning.

chapters.title: When the Summit Wakes
chapters.summary: A year later, Hazel and Mara fly a rented mail run over the same range, the glacier quiet and its secret buried. The summit catches the dawn; neither looks away. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: resolution — the mountain keeps its price, and they keep each other.
